verdicts.evidence: `c?.version` is only evaluated once `typeof c?.name === "string"` has succeeded, which already proves c is non-nullish, so the optional chain can never be the operand that saves the access. Measured: the full 75-case bench (including null, primitive and array components) and the 2500-comparison fuzz both show 0 differences, on a fuzz that flags the neighbouring name/version mutants.
